searchText: Feedback on whether I should switch reviewing strategies seemed to be mixed in the discussion above. I'm starting to lean toward just letting people do whatever they want in EIPs as long as the metadata is well formatted and the right sections exist (but I won't bother much for what is *in* the sections). I think this will overall reduce my workload, which has been struggling lately anyway. Which means I'll merge this despite the author violating most of the rules: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3540/files And I almost guarantee that half of those links are going to 404 within a year or two. I finally figured out the root of what was bothering me with the EIP that had trademark references in it: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3550#issuecomment-840965347 Curious to hear other people's thoughts on the matter. Root question is: If someone submitted an EIP that made a false legal claim, should we merge it? yeah that one is really bugging me Got it. I also updated the rational with backtesting for the three previous difficulty bomb sightings The first time the bomb will show up is Dec 7th (the bomb only bumps every 10000 blocks due to the calculations) https://etherscan.io/block/countdown/13800000 Which is in line with the target Dec 1st as we can get. Unless we go for the Nov-22 block which I wouldn't recommend welp, this whole thread was meant for ACD chat so... oh well. Automerger is working at least I was trying to hold myself back from commenting here, but I do not appreciate calling it out as "violating rules". I have explained my position there in several comments, for example in https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3540#issuecomment-841198049 Can you please explain what rules you are referring to? And I would prefer to have the answer on github so it is searchable and can be referenced later on for clarity. Unfortunately discord is ephemeral and in my opinion not good for discussions relating to EIP decisions. Unwritten (I think) rules that we have discussed in editor meetings that external links shouldn't be allowed/used. I think it is really bad practice enforcing unwritten rules and not letting people know what those are. Ideally they would be written rules, so nobody is confused. As you know, EIP editors are quite understaffed, so it is not uncommon for things to be discussed and decisions made without them making it into written form. (When I was more active I do not believe we enforced many unwritten rules, to be fair.) Usually we just start telling people the new thing during review, which works well in most cases because the majority of authors don't actually read the written instructions anyway. I think there are only 4-5 authors who are actually familiar with the written rules (mostly past EIP editors), which is usually when contention arises. FWIW, I think your distaste for this process is reasonable, and I think everyone wishes we had the manpower to do better. I really think enforcing strict rules for drafts is entirely pointless, given once it is merged as a draft, authors can do whatever they want. Nobody will be policing that. The next time it is policed when a status change is requested. Draft really was supposed to be enforcing that it fulfils the structure requirements, i.e. the header and existence of sections, but not the content. The content is reviewed during Review/Last Call/Final. The reason the no external link rule (and in fact most of the new rules) exist is because we don't have the manpower to do nuanced reviews, and strict rules are far easier to enforce than fuzzy rules. "No external links" vs "some external links". Editors are not supposed to do content reviews to this extent. It is the role of reviewers. Editors supposed to fulfil a role of structural checks, not content checks. I think given you are active on ACD you are chiming as a Reviewer too, but that is a distinct role from Editor. And mixing the two together is one source of contention. At least the above was original set up from the get go and was the way things went up until end of last year 🙂 Potentially this was revised but nobody ever documented the changes in these roles. This is the heart of the schism at the moment. Some believe that EIPs should be written as standards from start to finish and people should go elsewhere if they want a link repository. Others think that EIPs should be a place to discuss and collect data and links. Some think draft is one and final is the other, while others think all phases should be one or the other. I really disagreed with this approach when it was introduced around 2016 (i.e. merge draft as early as possible so it has a fixed URL), but it has been the process ever since then. And at this point maybe I am just used to it or it has grown on me. I think changing this process through "editor reviews" is not a good idea. It should be changed via revising EIP-1. I think everyone agrees that we **should** update EIP-1 when decisions are made. The problem is that it ends up getting dropped/forgotten because everyone involved is too busy. <@!301186049323958275> <@!543900561460822016> re: the trademark EIP: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3550#issuecomment-841247538 Eip-1 and getting ERCs seperated somehow. There is plenty of work, even if micah starts accepting every EIP. XD Easy access to the link here for merging when someone has got time <@!543900561460822016> <@!301186049323958275> https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3576 We got all the checks we need from AXIC, Vitalik, and I. But, the bot bugs on approving multiple files.
